key_insight: Trace ammonia in the feed poisons PEM fuel cells by lowering proton conductivity in the membrane and anode catalyst layer, which reduces current generation.
engineering_relevance: For ammonia-based hydrogen systems, controlling impurity level, temperature, humidity, and membrane thickness is critical to preserve fuel-cell efficiency.
method: Built a 3D numerical PEM fuel-cell model with ammonia impurities.
Simulated transport and poisoning effects under varying ammonia concentration, operating temperature, humidity, and membrane thickness.
Analyzed proton conductivity, current density, and dissolved water content to identify the poisoning mechanism.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter studies showing that higher temperature and humidity mitigate poisoning, while thinner membranes reduce poisoning but can make current distribution less uniform.
watch_item: Reducing membrane thickness may improve tolerance to ammonia but could introduce nonuniform current वितरण that complicates durability and design.
paper_title: Poisoning effect of ammonia on the performance and transport process of proton exchange membrane fuel cells
